behavior: This is an explicit behavioral co-repair of #1002 and all eight frozen #2811 cases, not permission for changed failure classifications. Settable nullable Int32 null and zero IDs must generate unique persisted integer keys and copy them back. Read-only Int32/ObjectId auto-ID InsertOne, InsertMany, UpsertOne and UpsertMany must either succeed coherently or fail before writes with a LiteException naming Id and explaining read-only/setter status. Preserve explicit-ID writes to immutable objects and ordinary writable Int32/Int64/Guid/ObjectId auto-generation; AutoId_Strong_Typed is a real independent passing control.

Keep the shared RemoveDocId/GetBsonDocs behavior consistent across Insert and Upsert. Do not broaden rejection to assigned IDs or mapped documents that do not need copy-back. No source-guard disposition, failure normalization extension or class-drift allowance is authorized.
compatibility: Preserve stored BSON key types, numeric sequence behavior, uniqueness, entity copy-back and existing explicit-ID rows. Inspect single and enumerable Insert/Upsert, including the obsolete InsertBulk wrapper; all reach the shared Insert.cs helpers except explicit-ID overloads. The frozen #2811 successful branch permits retaining a get-only entity ID unchanged, so explain the chosen public behavior instead of claiming it necessarily gains writable-ID semantics. Preserve ordinary v8 reopen and compatibility checks; no format change is authorized.
lifecycle: Mandatory prior finding from expansion-v8-1002 candidate a98b29089c01e21e50856abd0cc9bbea1ecc5631: a model with public int? Id { get; } and null ID threw NullReferenceException after Insert had committed; immediate and reopened counts were both one. Reproduce this exact get-only nullable-ID case on the new candidate and demonstrate either acknowledged coherent success or rejection with no durable write. Frozen #2811 uses non-nullable int and ObjectId, so passing it alone does not close this finding. Do not drop this obligation when starting a superseding campaign.

Validate writability before any engine mutation that can commit; never repair atomicity by write-then-delete compensation. Provide evidence for implicit and explicit transactions, caller Commit after catching rejection, unchanged pre-existing rows, and immediate plus independently reopened state. Check mixed/lazy batches with valid earlier items and an invalid later item: no prefix from a failed write call may remain commit-able or durable. Explain rollback effects on prior explicit-transaction work and avoid claiming per-call rollback preserves earlier work without evidence.

Attempt d600cab9aa8be419f0d3069a21bb5e03ff713307 only changed the error to InvalidOperationException and still failed all eight #2811 cases; it is not an accepted base or a completed repair. Use the current integrated base and fresh focused+broad evidence, retaining all original findings through three new reviews.

Assess every newly reachable post-engine ID copy-back failure, including a non-null custom setter that throws. A Setter != null guard alone does not prove safety for newly supported null nullable IDs. Demonstrate that no newly supported input can produce a durable failed call because assignment occurs after commit; review both single and enumerable paths and require rollback-safe placement or an equivalent justified design.

finding.summary: A get-only nullable integer ID throws after its insert has already committed
finding.evidence: Candidate line 96 newly removes a null Int32 _id and returns removed=true. Insert(T) then calls _engine.Insert at line 20; Engine/Engine/Transaction.cs lines 89-92 commit and release the auto-transaction before control returns. Only afterward, Insert.cs line 27 invokes _id.Setter. Client/Mapper/Reflection/Reflection.Expression.cs lines 52-53 deliberately return a null setter for a get-only property, so this invocation throws NullReferenceException after commit. An executed net8.0 candidate repro using `public int? Id { get; }` produced `exception=System.NullReferenceException`, `immediate-count=1`, and `reopened-count=1`. At the base SHA the changed predicate leaves the null _id in place, so Engine/Engine/Insert.cs rejects id.IsNull inside AutoTransaction before storage and rolls back. The candidate therefore turns a failed call into a durable, caller-unacknowledged write. Validate writability before entering the engine or otherwise ensure ID copy-back cannot fail after commit.
